newsitem.title: USA: Sanofi unit sues firm over HIV-2 test kit.
newsitem.headline: Sanofi unit sues firm over HIV-2 test kit.

text.p: A U.S. subsidiary of France's Sanofi, Genetic Systems Corp, has sued United Biomedical Inc of Hauppauge, N.Y., for alleged infringement of a patent for an HIV-2 virus test kit.

In papers filed in the U.S. District Court in Delaware, Genetic said it was the exclusive licensee of the Institut Pasteur '391 patent "for detecting the presence or absence of human immunodeficiency viruses type 2 (HIV-2) which cause...AIDS."
The Institut Pasteur is also a plaintiff in the lawsuit and an inventor of the patent, Luc Montagnier, is credited with the discovery of the HIV-2 virus.
In an affidavit, Genetic president Terrance Bieker said the HIV kits are half of the company's business and have totaled more than $20 million in sales since they were introduced in 1990 and 1991.
"Between Genetic Systems and (sublicensee) Abbott (Laboratories Inc), all customer needs in the U.S. for HIV-2 diagnostic kits are satisfied," Bieker said.
He claims that competition from United Biomedical's kits would reduce Genetic's follow-on sales of other products to its HIV kit customers.

Genetic has asked Judge Joseph Farnan for a preliminary injunction that would block United Biomedical from marketing its trademark test kit UBI-HIV 1/2 EIA in the U.S. That kit received U.S. Food and Drug Administration approval in January. An employee of United Biomedical told Reuters distribution of the kits was on hold but did not know why.
United Biomedical plans to distribute its kit through Biochem Immunosystems (US) Inc, a division of BioChem Pharma Inc, court papers say.

United Biomedical must respond to the genetic motion for a preliminary injunction by April 7. A Genetic spokesman would not comment on whether the companies are in talks. United Biomedical declined any comment.
